architect.rationale: Two independent reasons, either one sufficient. (1) FILE OVERLAP, independent of isolation: four of the five work items must edit graph_agents/CURRENT-STATE.md (changelog / gap #1 correction / gap #7 closure / decisions row) and two must edit graph_agents/GRAPH.md (S3 state contract, S2 stop-rule note on degraded mode). Per architect.md:18-24 and GRAPH.md:84, slices that touch the same files are not a diamond, they are a sequence. I cannot name 3 disjoint file sets here, so it is not a diamond. (2) NO ISOLATION, NO ROLLBACK: scout facts 3+4 confirm neither repos/ nor graph_agents/ is a git repo, so feature-graph/SKILL.md:63 isolation worktree is unexecutable and architect.md:28 (one slice = one builder = one branch) is unsatisfiable for this target. Even after s1 creates a repo, this run would be the first-ever execution of builder/reviewer/integrator (CURRENT-STATE gap #2) AND a self-modification of the agent definitions the orchestrator spawns from. Proving worktrees, proving three untested nodes, and rewriting the spawn definitions in one run is stacking three unvalidated things on each other. Single-loop, sequential, one commit per slice.

The logged decision (CURRENT-STATE.md:114) is 'Holding company, not monorepo - each app its own git repo', and CLAUDE.md:3-4 says repos/ is deliberately not a repo. The stated reason is that a root repo would swallow all five apps into a monorepo. graph_agents/ is itself a node in the portfolio graph (CLAUDE.md:41-43, GRAPH.md:18-20) and contains zero app code, so giving it its own repo is the SAME rule every other node already follows, not an exception to it. repos/ stays un-repo'd and s1 asserts that as a done_when check.

isolation_decision.c_snapshot_copy_rejected: A copy-the-directory substitute reintroduces every problem git worktrees solve (merge, conflict detection, diff) with none of the tooling, and it is a second mechanism to maintain forever. Once s1 lands, real worktrees are available for FUTURE fleet runs; this run does not need them because it is single-loop.
isolation_decision.a_force_single_loop_partially_adopted: Adopted as a standing rule for any run whose target is .claude/agents/** or .claude/skills/** - not because of git (s1 fixes that) but because of self-modification. Written into feature-graph/SKILL.md by s5.
isolation_decision.what_happens_when_a_builder_corrupts_an_: Before s1: nothing. The file is gone and must be retyped from memory. That is exactly why s1 runs first and alone, before any agent file is touched. After s1: `git -C graph_agents checkout -- .claude/agents/<file>.md` restores one file and `git -C graph_agents reset --hard HEAD` restores the whole fleet. The builder commits after each slice, so the blast radius of any single bad edit is one slice.

self_modification_protocol.rule: The plan is correct under BOTH answers because no slice's correctness depends on an edited definition taking effect during this run. s2 rewrites architect.md/reviewer.md/ops.md and s5 touches feature-graph/SKILL.md; no later slice in this run spawns an architect, an ops node, or re-enters the skill. The only agent spawned after s2 is the reviewer for the whole loop, and it reviews a DIFF - it reads the new reviewer.md as data either way, and its verdict does not change depending on which copy of its own definition was loaded at session start. Concretely: builder.md is edited by exactly one slice (s3) and only additively (record a branch field), so the question 'does a later builder see the new builder.md' never becomes load-bearing.

Do not assume this session is running the definitions now on disk.

plan.intent: Close gap #7 with machinery instead of more prose. Write graph_agents/.graph/verify-state.py: it takes a run-id (or a path to a state.json) plus one or more required node key names, and exits 0 only if every named key exists AND is non-empty - where a dict whose values are all empty strings or empty lists counts as NOT written, which is exactly the current shape of the untouched integrator key. architect.edges: STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL s1 -> s2 -> s3 -> s4 -> s5. One builder, one context, one commit per slice. s1 -> everything: the real artifact is the git repo plus the initial commit, which is the ONLY rollback path for every later edit; nothing may edit a fleet file before it exists. s2 and s3 -> s5: the real artifact is the changed agent and schema files that the CURRENT-STATE.md changelog and gap list must describe - writing the snapshot before the changes exist would make it fiction. s4 -> s5: the real artifact is verify-state.py, which must exist on disk before GRAPH.md section 3 and gap #7 can point at it. Honest note on fake edges: s2, s3 and s4 have nearly disjoint file sets and would be parallel if isolation existed. They are ordered here because there is one builder and no isolation, so ordering costs nothing and removes the last collision surface. s1 and s5 are real edges; the s2/s3/s4 ordering is a degraded-mode concession and is labelled as such rather than dressed up as a dependency.
not_doing: NOT enforcing the umbrella invariant (gap #5). A cross-app-import linter is real engineering with its own design questions - which languages, what counts as an import, where it runs with no CI - and it is about APPS, not about the agent graph. It deserves its own run. Explicitly out of scope.

NOT running a diamond to prove diamonds work. Gaps #2 and #3 stay open on purpose. Proving fan-out belongs on a real app with a real git repo and a real test suite - huntstack - not on the fleet own definitions.

NOT touching the staleness hook or flag-stale-state.py. CURRENT-STATE.md:119 records a user-confirmed decision that it flags and never auto-stamps. Not revisiting it, not extending it, not making it block.
NOT adding, removing, renaming or re-tiering any node. Six nodes stay six nodes, scout stays haiku, nothing is downgraded, and no new critic or planner node is invented.

NOT rewriting architect.md wholesale. Judged honestly: its shape logic (lines 11-24), its delete-fake-edges rule and its Return block are sound and were load-bearing in this very run. Its real defects are exactly three - no state contract, a false claim about branches, and a done_when rule with no answer for Markdown - and s2 fixes those three. A rewrite would churn a file that mostly works.
NOT changing human gate placement or adding new gates.
NOT creating a git remote, pushing, or making repos/ a git repository. s1 explicitly asserts repos/ is still not a repo.
NOT touching anything outside graph_agents/. None of the five app repos are read or modified by any slice.
NOT building a snapshot-copy isolation mechanism (option c). Rejected with reasons recorded in isolation_decision.

NOT resolving whether Claude Code reloads agent definitions mid-session (scout risk 6). The plan is designed to be correct under either answer instead of depending on the answer. Resolving it is a separate experiment run.
NOT auto-updating CURRENT-STATE.md Last verified without a real re-check.
NOT touching portfolio/registry.json or the new-app skill.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK, so s5 does not oversell it: (1) it does not check CONTENT CORRECTNESS -- a node that writes {"status":"done"} into builders.s9 with no changed list passes, because a dict with one non-empty value is non-empty; (2) it does not check the key SHAPE against _schema.json -- wrong fields, missing `branch`, missing `verdict` all pass; (3) it does not check WHO wrote the key, so it cannot detect the contract violation it is named after -- one node rewriting another node's key is invisible to it, and the orchestrator hand-writing every key still passes; (4) it does not check that the key matches the work -- a stale key from a previous attempt passes; (5) numbers and booleans count as non-empty by design, so `{"gated": false}` passes; (6) it is advisory, not enforcing: nothing invokes it automatically, no hook fires it, and it exits 1 in a skill step the orchestrator has to actually choose to run. It is a check, not a gate. DESIGN NOTE: emptiness is recursive -- a dict or list whose values are ALL empty is empty, which is exactly what makes the integrator negative test work. Run path resolves from the script's own location (graph_agents/.graph/runs/<id>/state.json), so it works from repos/ or anywhere; a direct path to a state.json is also accepted as the first argument.
